Testimony of Lt. Bruce Scott
IN SUPPORT or LD 1568
An Act to Allow the Use of a Siren in a Vehicle Used by a Harbor
Master or Deputy Harbor Master

Senator Nangle, Rep. Crafts, and distinguished Members of the ]oint
Standing Committee on Transportation, my name is Lt. Bruce Scott, and I am the Commanding Officer of the State Police Traffic Safety Unit. I am
here today to testify on behalf of the Department of Public Safety and the
Maine State Police in Support of LD 1568 as amended.

In 2.023 the law was amended to allow privately owned vehicles operated by Harbor Masters and Deputy Harbor Masters to display red/white lights when responding to watercraft emergencies, similar to that of volunteer
firefighters.
Shawn Hebert, Treasurer of the State of Maine Harbor Master's Association,
reached out to me a few months ago and asked if the Department of Public
Safety and the Maine State Police would support a bill that would allow municipalities to use sirens in addition to their red and white lights in the vehicles owned by the municipalities that were used to respond to watercraft emergencies. The original language of this bill, as drafted, would have allowed all Harbor Masters and Deputy Harbor Masters to use a siren in addition to their currently authorized red and white lights in their
personally owned vehicles.

I made Shawn Hebert and Rep. Ankeles aware of our concerns with the
original drafting of the bill as it would allow sirens in non-emergency vehicles. Rep. Ankeles and Mr. Hebert both indicated that the original language of the bill was not their intent, and they quickly went to work with Melanie, your committee analyst, and drafted an amendment.
This amendment adds language that expands to the definition of an emergency vehicle, a vehicle owned by a municipality operated by a Harbor
Master or Deputy Harbor Master used to respond to watercraft emergencies.
It further allows a siren to be used in these emergency vehicles when in route to an actual emergency and when operated by a Harbor Master or Deputy Harbor Master who has successfully completed a State of Maine Emergency Operator' s Course. With these amendments, we fully support
this bill and recognize the importance of timely responses to watercraft
emergencies.
For these reasons, we urge you to vote in favor of LD 1568.
On behalf of the Department of Public Safety and the Maine State Police, I
thank you for your time and would be happy to try and answer any questions that you might have.

Testimony ofRep. Dan Ankeles presenting

LD 1568, An Act to Allow the Use of a Siren in a Vehicle Used by a

Before the Joint Standing Committee on Transportation

Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts and fellow members of the Joint Standing Committee on
Transportation, thank you for the opportunity to share testimony with you. I am still Representative Dan Ankeles, and I serve House District 100, which is a central portion of
Brunswick. It's my pleasure to present LD 1568, An Act to Allow the Use of a Siren in a
Vehicle Used by a Harbor Master or Deputy Harbor Master.
Almost three weeks after cloture, the Maine Harbor Masters Association reached out to me to see
if it was too late to make a small change to the law so that harbor masters could use sirens when responding to an emergency situation. This is something that apparently was supposed to happen in a previous Legislature but was inadvertently left out.

I had no idea this was even an issue until it was brought to me, but all of you know that
supporting good working waterfront policy is very important to me and to my constituents. We
have one of the most productive sets of clam flats in the state, a growing and very well-respected
oyster farming industry and all kinds of other people who spend a lot of time out on the water.
Part of our job is to do what we can to keep them safe.

I'll note that I've attached a sponsor amendment to my testimony, and I will be speaking to the
amended version and not the original text.

As amended, this bill adds a vehicle owned by a municipality and used by a harbor master to the list of authorized emergency vehicles. The amendment also requires a municipality or agency to
require a person appointed or reappointed as a harbor master or deputy harbor master to have completed a State of Maine emergency vehicle operator's course if operating a vehicle while
exercising emergency privileges.

The reason you've got an amended version before you is because the State Police found some language they were uncomfortable with, and working with the harbor masters and our intrepid
committee analyst, we were able to make some edits and still accomplish the intent of the bill. I
want to particularly thank Lt. Bruce Scott for his hard work to get this bill in good shape prior to
this hearing.

using sirens.
Thank you for the opportunity to present this bill. I am happy to answer questions.

Testimony of the Maine Municipal Association
In Opposition To
LD 1568 - An Act to Allow the Use of a Siren in a Vehicle Used by a Harbor Master or Deputy Harbor Master
May 1, 2025
Sen. Nangle, Rep. Crafts, and distinguished members of the Transportation Committee, my name is Rebecca Graham, and I am submitting testimony in opposition to LD 1568 at the direction of MMA's Legislative Policy Committee (LPC). Our LPC is made up of individuals from across Maine with municipal officials elected by their peers across Maine's 35 Senate districts representing communities with very different access to available enforcement resources and local capacity.
As drafted, the bill would allow the addition of a siren to a personal vehicle operated by a harbor master or deputy harbor master and permit its use when responding to a watercraft emergency. A siren is currently not possible to be placed in a personal vehicle with good reason as it increases the level of risk incurred by a municipality for operation and actions that are outside the scope of municipal control such as damage to a personal vehicle occurring during a response which is increased when the vehicle operated is not easily identifiable as an emergency response vehicle.
Additionally, vehicles with lights installed are not allowed to exceed the posted speed limit and the installation of a siren with lights is generally necessary when a response is at a higher rate of speed. Harbor masters are not all fully certified law enforcement officers with emergency vehicle operation training and usually trained to a lower green pin level. Emergency vehicle operation training is an important skill that in part preserves the public safety of others who are in the path of response.
While municipal officials appreciate the permissive aspects of the bill, the current restriction in place affords them the ability to make sure any emergency response is in a clearly identifiable public safety vehicle with regular maintenance and with clear municipal purpose. As drafted, officials will be pressured to accept the liability of operation in personal vehicles that may cost far more to repair than a basic municipal vehicle and lack any markings that would provide confidence for other operators that yielding to a non-standard vehicle with lights and siren is for a genuine emergency purpose. This is also important because secondary accidents occurring from yielding to emergency response vehicles are frequent and adds to municipal liability.
For all of these reasons, officials ask the committee to consider the significant pressure that will be placed on officials to approve these additional installations in personal vehicles and recognize that approving this for harbor masters will increase the likelihood that fire fighters and police officers will submit similar legislation in the future. Officials believe this type of emergency equipment may be better suited for installation in municipally owned, maintained, and clearly marked vehicles and require additional training that is not part of the current certification process.
